title: Aegis Override Log Entry
description: Schema for a single line in .agentpolicy/state/overrides.jsonl. The file is NDJSON — one JSON object per line, append-only. Each line records a policy-significant event that belongs in the audit trail: a human-authorized override, a refused or blocked attempt, a silently-logged compliance, a runtime event such as construction mode activation, or any other event a conforming implementation chooses to record. Any Aegis-compatible tool that writes to this log must produce entries conforming to this schema so auditors and other agents can interpret the log regardless of which implementation wrote it.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the entry was written.

policy_violated.description: Identifier of the policy or event the entry concerns. Implementations typically use a namespaced form such as 'principle:<id>', 'convention:<id>', 'permission:<category>', or a tool-specific marker like 'construction_mode:start'. The exact namespace vocabulary is left to implementations; what the spec requires is that the value identifies what this entry is about so the log can be searched and grouped.

human_confirmed.description: Whether the human explicitly confirmed this entry. True when a human authorized an override after being shown the policy violation. Typically false for blocked attempts, silently-logged compliance, or runtime markers — implementations set this according to their own behavior model.

agent_role.description: Which role the agent was operating as at the moment this entry was written.

rationale.description: Why this entry exists. For a human-authorized override, the human's stated reason. For a blocked attempt, the reason the action was refused. For a runtime event, a summary of what the event represents. Implementations may use this field for any contextual narrative the audit trail benefits from.

policy_text.description: Optional: full text of the policy that the entry concerns, so the log is self-contained and readable without cross-referencing the policy files as they existed at the time.

action_requested.description: Optional: what the human (or another agent) instructed when the entry was created. Most relevant for override and refusal entries.
